questions.text: Which of the following is a type of a out-of-order execution, with the reordering done by a compiler
questions.solution:
Software pipelining reorders instructions from different loop iterations so they overlap, which is out-of-order execution arranged by the compiler. Loop unrolling, dead code elimination and strength reduction do not reorder execution this way.

Answer: software pipelining

questions.text:
Given the grammar
[latex]s \rightarrow T^{*} S \mid T[/latex]
[latex]T \rightarrow U+T \mid U[/latex]
[latex]U \rightarrow a \mid b[/latex]
Which of the following statements is wrong?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- One production per level and right recursion [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not ambiguous.
- + is generated lower in the tree (in T) than * (in S) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] + has higher priority.
- Both rules are right recursive [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] right-to-left grouping.

All three statements are correct, so none of them is wrong.

Answer: None of these

questions.text: Which one indicates a technique of building cross compilers?
questions.solution:
The Canadian cross builds a cross compiler using three different machines: the compiler is built on machine A, runs on machine B, and produces code for machine C.

Answer: Canadian cross

questions.text: In a two-pass assembler, resolution of subroutine calls and inclusion of labels in the symbol table is done during
questions.solution:
In a two-pass assembler:
- Pass 1 scans the program, assigns addresses and enters every label into the symbol table.
- Pass 2 uses the completed symbol table to resolve references, including calls to subroutines defined later (forward references).

So resolution of subroutine calls happens in the second pass and inclusion of labels in the first pass.

Answer: second pass and first pass respectively
